title: Jira Workload
description: Tile: Jira Workload. Same data points as Jira's own native Workload report -- Agent, Work Items In Progress -- for one Jira project, scoped via an explicit `project_key` the same way Jira's own Workload report itself is a per-project report, not a site-wide one. **Redesigned (per the tile owner's explicit request) from a flat two-column `Table` into a per-agent card list, visually modeled on `xero-practice-manager`'s `xero-pm-team-schedule-demo` ("Team Schedule (Demo)") tile** -- initials avatar, name + status line, a colored `ProgressBar`, and a status `Badge` per row, separated by `Divider`s -- but wired to this connector's own real, live `search_issues` data, not hardcoded demo values. That XPM tile is 100% static (no `dataProvider`) and its per-row layout is a plugin-scoped composite component (`xero-practice-manager/StaffRow`) -- neither is reachable or appropriate here (plugin-elements are scoped per-plugin, and this redesign deliberately avoids adding a new composite of its own), so the row is instead hand-rolled directly in this widget's spec from system components (`Avatar`, `Row`, `Stack`, `Badge`, `ProgressBar`, `Divider`, `Text`) via a `repeat` over `/ui/workload` -- consistent with `TILE-DISPLAY-STANDARDS.md` §6's guidance that a per-record card row (not tabular, multi-column data) is exactly the hand-roll case `Table` isn't meant for. **Status thresholds and tone mapping (confirmed decisions, not a guess), based on the same in-progress `count` this tile already computes:** 0 -> "Available" (`muted`), 1-4 -> "On track" (`success`), 5+ -> "Overloaded" (`destructive`). `warning` is deliberately unused -- per §7's restraint principle, this is a 3-state field. `muted` for "Available" is a deliberate departure from the XPM demo tile's own choice of `warning`/amber for the same concept: having spare capacity isn't a bad state worth flagging, unlike an agent already overloaded. **Workload bar:** `count` scaled so 5 in-progress items reads as a full (100%) bar, capped there (`Math.min(100, (count / 5) * 100)`) -- an agent with 11 items reads the same "maxed out" as one with 6, both already past a sustainable load. **Second line, in place of the XPM demo's per-person "role" (e.g. "Senior Accountant"):** Jira's `search_issues` assignee data (`{ accountId, displayName, accountType }`) has no job-title/role concept at all, and none of this connector's other tools resolve one either -- rather than fabricate a role, this line shows only the honest, singular/plural-aware count phrase ("1 work item in progress" / "4 work items in progress"). **Avatar initials** are derived client-side from `displayName` -- first letter of the first word + first letter of the last word, uppercased (e.g. "Sean Baker" -> "SB"); a single-word name takes its own first two letters instead. **Divider trade-off, disclosed rather than hidden:** the widgets-system's `repeat` has no `$last`/`$index` construct to conditionally skip a trailing separator (confirmed absent from `apps/web/src/features/widgets-system/system/components.tsx`), so each row's `Divider` is part of its own repeated template -- meaning the final row also gets a trailing divider before the truncation note / card edge, unlike the XPM demo's hand-placed dividers which stop after the second-to-last row. A cosmetic, accepted trade-off, not an oversight. Row click-through is preserved exactly as before, just moved off `Table`'s `rowAction.fromRow` onto the repeated `Row`'s own `on.click` (`open_url`, wrapped through the `identity` computed helper on `{"$item": "searchUrl"}` -- a bare `$item` inside an action param resolves to a state PATH, not its value, the same gotcha already documented and worked around on this plugin's Service Desk Queue tile's `requestRow`): clicking an agent still opens Jira's own issue navigator (`https://<site>/issues/?jql=...`) pre-filtered to that agent's own in-progress work in this project (`assignee = "<accountId>" AND project = <project_key> AND statusCategory = "In Progress"`). The full URL is still pre-built per row inside `atlassian_workload_by_agent` itself (as a `searchUrl` field), not computed at click time. `site_url`/`project_key` are both plain literal args passed into that function (hardcoded to the sandbox, `https://mysmb.atlassian.net` / `KAN`) -- same per-tenant-manual-edit limitation already accepted for `service_desk_id`/`project_key` everywhere else in this connector; there's no cheap way to resolve a browsable site URL from within a single dataProvider call. Built entirely on the existing `search_issues` tool (JQL `project = <project_key> AND statusCategory = "In Progress"`, `fields: ["assignee"]`, `max_results: 100`) -- no new server-side tool needed. `atlassian_workload_by_agent` (this plugin's widget-elements) groups the returned issues by `fields.assignee.accountId`, counting one work item per issue, and returns them sorted most-work-items-first, each row now also carrying `statusLabel`/`statusTone`/`loadPercent`/`initials`/`countLabel` alongside the original `accountId`/`displayName`/`count`/`searchUrl`. Two exclusions, both per the ticket's explicit ask for 'only human user accounts': issues with a `null` assignee (unassigned -- doesn't belong to anyone's workload) are dropped entirely, and any assignee whose `accountType` isn't `"atlassian"` (Atlassian's own Jira Cloud Platform REST API v3 User resource docs: `"atlassian"` = real human user, `"app"` = Connect/Forge/automation account, `"customer"` = JSM-only customer account) is excluded as a non-human 'inbuilt agent'. **Honesty note, not a hedge to gloss over:** the exclusion path itself (`accountType !== "atlassian"`) is UNTESTED against a live example -- this sandbox has an 'Automatic' account that appears in Jira's assignee-picker UI but could not actually be assigned to a real issue through that UI (selecting it silently reverted to Unassigned), so there was no way to produce a real non-"atlassian"-accountType assignee to confirm this filter against. Only the human-agent path (accountType `"atlassian"`) was confirmed live. See `atlassian_workload_by_agent`'s own JSDoc in `widget-elements/src/index.ts` for the full reasoning, including a 2019 Atlassian Developer Community report of `accountType` sometimes misreporting app accounts as `"atlassian"` (unconfirmed whether still current). Capped at 20 rows per `TILE-DISPLAY-STANDARDS.md` §11 (irrelevant in practice for a single project's human-agent roster, kept for consistency). `search_issues` defaults to 50 results, capped at 100 max, paginated via `nextPageToken` -- a widget's `dataProvider` fires exactly one call, so this tile requests the max (`max_results: 100`) and checks the response's `isLast` flag: when `false`, more In-Progress issues exist beyond the 100 fetched, and the tile discloses that plainly (per §13's data-governance veracity principle, the same honesty pattern as the SLA%-this-month action's own truncation disclosure) rather than presenting a partial per-agent count as complete.

props.message: No in-progress work items assigned to a human agent on this project.

props.text: 100+ issues found — showing a partial count (more exist beyond the first 100 fetched).
